summary.headline: Oil India FY26: consolidated income Rs 38,981 cr (+3% YoY), PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%), with Rs 11.5/share dividend repeated.
summary.overview: Oil India's annual investors' meet (25 May 2026, transcript filed 29 May) covered FY26 results, a record 74-well drilling year and a 1.6x GRM uplift at subsidiary NRL. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 13,498 cr (+5%) and PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%) despite crude realisation falling to $69/bbl from $78. Production was 6.64 MMtoe, with about 0.1 MMt lost to a 10-15 day economic blockade. Management reiterated the 9 MMTPA NRL expansion by March 2027, a roughly 100-well-a-year drilling plan, and offshore exploration reliant on the Samudra Manthan Mission for deep-water wells.

financial_highlights.change: ~60% drilling, ~25% capital projects, ~13% investments in subsidiaries/JVs
Down from $78; lowest in last 5 years

segments.name: Upstream (Oil India)
segments.commentary: Production 6.64 MMtoe (3.45 MMt oil, 3.15 BCM gas); daily crude peaked at ~81,354 bpd, with management citing 82,200+ bpd as of late May. Record 74 wells drilled (22 exploration, 52 development) and 307 workovers. 2P reserve replacement ratio 1.20 (vs 0.94) on 231 MMt reserves, 31-year reserve life.

segments.name: Midstream (pipelines)
segments.commentary: Numaligarh-Siliguri product pipeline expanded from 1.72 to 5.5 MMTPA, completed at Rs 750 crore vs Rs 860 crore approved outlay; PM inaugurated 13 March 2026. Duliajan-Numaligarh gas pipeline expanded from 1.2 to 2.5 MMSCMD, mechanically complete, awaiting a ~7-day NRL shutdown to commission.

segments.name: Downstream (NRL, 100% subsidiary of Oil India Ltd, 3 MMTPA)
segments.commentary: Record 103% crude throughput, 99.1% availability, 87.25% distillate yield and 727 TMT MS output; GRM 1.6x prior year. Navratna status conferred Dec 2025. Expansion to 9 MMTPA targeted for March 2027, with polypropylene unit on track; expansion capex ~Rs 46,000 crore including ~Rs 7,200 crore for PPU.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Mozambique force majeure lifted Nov 2025; two LNG trains of 13 MMTPA targeted for end-2028 or early 2029, with ~$1.8 billion committed and ~$300 million cost escalation pending CCEA approval. Russian assets (Taas, Vankor) have returned ~$1 billion in dividends. Libya 95/96 major commercial discovery.

segments.name: New energy and others
segments.commentary: Oil India Green Energy Ltd (wholly-owned) has ~2 GW renewable capacity in JVs pipeline and 2 CBG plants under construction, with 2 more awarded or in tender, against a target of 25 by 2030. 49 KTPA bamboo 2G ethanol plant inaugurated Sept 2025; NRL green hydrogen plant of 2.4 KTPA (Rs 138 crore) due by end-2026.

guidance_outlook: Production: 4 MMtoe achievable with ~100 wells drilled per year; long-term target 12 MMtoe by 2030 (from 10).
Gas: 3.35 BCM guided for FY27; ~5 BCM targeted by FY28 once Duliajan feeder line and DNPL expansion are commissioned.
NRL: CDU/VDU ~mid-July 2026 (~400 TMT output after that, mostly diesel), DHDT about a month later, PFCC/RPTU by Dec-Jan, full 9 MMTPA by March 2027 (stabilised by March 2028).
Capex: rollover of ~Rs 10,000 crore a year for ~100 onshore wells per year, plus shallow-water offshore drilling.

Offshore: deep-water well targeted for spud around June 2027; four-plus-four deep-water wells at ~Rs 1,200 crore each (Rs 4,800-5,000 crore), contingent on Samudra Manthan Mission sponsorship. Shallow-water wells ~Rs 800 crore each.
NRL excise duty: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26, with 50% NE excise benefit and no sunset clause at 9 MMTPA; management expects calibration if FOB HSD prices fall.
capex_capacity: Drilling: 74 wells in FY26 (record); released drillable location inventory ~218 vs ~45 earlier; average Assam shelf depth ~4,300 m.

Offshore: deepest well (6,000 m, Kerala-Konkan) at ~3,400 m; Andaman well 3 drilling complete and testing; KG DSF appraisal well underway; gas occurrence in Andaman well 2 under appraisal with 600 sq km 3D seismic.
Feeder/evacuation: Duliajan feeder line (3.5 MMSCMD) authorised; PNGRB approval Feb 2026, mechanical completion FY28, offtake up 40%.
Gas capacity: production ~8 MMSCMD, ramp-up path to 13-15 MMSCMD with 15-18 pure gas wells identified.
Crude import pipeline Paradip-Numaligarh (9 MMTPA) 92% physically complete as of 30 April 2026; 99% ROU acquired.
demand_pricing: Realisation: crude at $69/bbl in FY26, lowest in 5 years; government moves on royalty and post-wellhead cost realisation cited as cash-flow support.

New well gas: 1.5 MMSCMD allocated to NRL, priced at 20% premium over APM, but only accrues once NRL is commissioned and allocation is confirmed; allocation priority runs CGD, fertiliser, refinery/petchem, then power.
Gas to NE CGD: ~50,000 SCMD allocated to NE Gas Distribution and Purbabharati Gas Distribution as NRL reseller.
Product demand: management cites 7-8% growth in refined product consumption; NRL export via Indo-Bangladesh pipeline optional, not the basis for 9 MMTPA.
Competition/partners: TotalEnergies signed technology service agreement (Nov 2025) for offshore seismic and exploration support, with a say in investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offshore exploration capex and how will the capability gap be addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shallow-water well ~Rs 800 crore; deep-water wells ~Rs 1,200 crore each, four plus four wells (~Rs 4,800-5,000 crore), contingent on Samudra Manthan sponsorship. Government also identified Rs 3,200 crore for four stratigraphic wells jointly with ONGC.

qa_highlights.question: NRL excise duty benefit in FY26 and impact of recent duty cut?
qa_highlights.answer: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26; no sunset clause on 50% NE excise benefit at 9 MMTPA. Management expects excise to be recalibrated against HSD FOB prices if they fall.

qa_highlights.question: NRL 9 MMTPA viability, and terms of the TotalEnergies arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Viability rests on domestic demand (7-8% growth) and NE/mainland logistics, with Panchgram, Singimari and Jogighopa depots and Siliguri tankage. TotalEnergies is a service agreement, with Total able to weigh in on investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: NRL timelines, first product output, and capex spent/remaining?
qa_highlights.answer: Mother units by end-July; ~400 TMT output after that, mostly diesel. Full 9 MMT by March 2027, stabilised March 2028. Expansion capex ~Rs 46,000 crore including PPU (Rs 7,200 crore).

qa_highlights.question: FY27 production, gas and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: 4 MMT with 100 wells; gas 3.35 BCM in FY27 and ~5 BCM 18 months out. Rollover capex ~Rs 10,000 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Current production exit rate and gas ramp path?
qa_highlights.answer: Current crude ~82,200 bpd, a record. Gas ~8 MMSCMD now; management says 13-15 MMSCMD possible with new pipelines, with first accrual only on allocation and commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Mozambique incremental equity outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: ~$1.8 billion already committed; ~$300 million escalation pending CCEA. Further phases to be assessed after FID.

risks_watch: Samudra Manthan Mission notification and sponsorship mechanism still pending; deep-water capex is uncertain until notified.
NRL expansion timeline: DNPL commissioning depends on a 7-day NRL shutdown deferred by Middle East crisis; CDU/VDU mechanical completion due mid-July 2026.
New well gas premium (20%) depends on government allocation; accrual timing tied to CGD saturation in NE.
Excise benefit (~Rs 3,000 crore in FY26) may be recalibrated if product prices fall.
Production risk from economic blockades (lost ~0.1 MMt in FY26) and natural decline of 10-12% a year.
Mozambique cost escalation (~$300 million) awaiting CCEA approval.
key_quotes: Dr. Ranjit Rath, Chairman and Managing Director, Oil India Limited and Chairman of Numaligarh Refinery Limited.

The idea is that through a mechanism while the data collection in terms of 2D and 3D seismic data will be sponsored by the Government, the Government would also sponsor the deep water and ultra deep water wells which we intend to drill in our exploration acreage.

So, we would really come to know once it is notified, how many numbers of wells government is going to sponsor 100%, how many wells government is going to sponsor 50% or precisely how the mechanism would be.
So, excise to my opinion is going to get calibrated based on the overall FOB of HSD which is the driving force for the refinery transfer price which happens between NRL and the OMCs.
Now the question is this New well gas needs to be allocated by government.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on production records, NRL commissioning and offshore ambition, repeatedly stressing government support and "on track" delivery. Cautious or evasive on Samudra Manthan Mission mechanics, deep-water well sponsorship terms, and NRL excise recalibration, which management repeatedly deferred until notification or government approval.

adds.what: NRL refinery expansion 3 to 9 MMTPA (~400 TMT first phase CDU/VDU)

growth.why: Management guides 4 MMtoe production in FY27 on 100 wells and gas at 3.35 BCM, with NRL's 3 to 9 MMTPA expansion targeted by March 2027 (capex ~Rs 46,000 cr); the NRL and drilling plans have capacity and capex behind them, but the 9 MMTPA date and well-count targets still depend on commissioning steps and Samudra Manthan sponsorship for offshore.
